§7.3.8 Redacted Text

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-redacted-text · text marks

✅ Normative

Each contiguous redacted span MUST be rendered as one [REDACTED] marker, in the position the suppressed text occupied. Visible text and any printed exemption code MUST be kept; the hidden characters and their count MUST NOT be inferred.

Text blacked out or boxed over in the source document.

The rendering

The marker sits where the suppressed text was, so the surrounding line still reads correctly:

Account holder: [REDACTED]

Where only part of a value is covered, the marker MUST replace only the covered part, and the visible characters MUST be kept verbatim — not normalised, padded or reconstructed. Printed masking characters are visible characters, escaped where they are Markdown syntax (see Escaping Printed Marks§7.2.4):

Account number: \*\*\*\*-\*\*\*\*-\*\*\*\*-4471

When boxes are requested, a redacted span has a box like any other printed region — see Boxes and Granularity§3.3.

Why a positive marker beats silence

A redaction is an assertion: something was here and was deliberately removed. If the output emits nothing, a reader cannot tell "the field was blank" from "the field was suppressed" — a meaningful difference in a legal or regulatory document.

[REDACTED] is the same bracketed-placeholder shape used for Signatures§7.3.10 ([signature]) and for QR Codes and Bar Codes§7.3.7 (![](QR Code)).

✅ Sample — a redaction bar inside a sentence

One black bar where the appellant's name was, between filed by and , against the response of the. The bold case number and council name on either side are printed and kept.

Expected Markdown

HAVING SEEN the electronic file formed on account of the appeal for review 04871/OTAIP/AR/2018 filed by [REDACTED] , against the response of the Municipal Council of Puente Alvara, the following resolution is hereby issued.

Markdown source
HAVING SEEN the electronic file formed on account of the appeal for review **04871/OTAIP/AR/2018** filed by [REDACTED] , against the response of the **Municipal Council of Puente Alvara**, the following resolution is hereby issued.

✅ Sample — a redaction bar inside a transcript line

Line 4: Was ████ paying that before? — one black bar in the middle of a question, the rest of the page untouched. The transcript lines follow Transcript Pages§6.11.

Expected Markdown · excerpt, lines 1–5

83

A My delivery van insurance. Q And what's that? A $150 a month. Q Was [REDACTED] paying that before? A Yes, he was.

…

Markdown source
83


A My delivery van insurance.
Q And what's that?
A $150 a month.
Q Was [REDACTED] paying that before?
A Yes, he was.


<!-- … -->

Exemption codes

A redacted region that prints an exemption code MUST be rendered as [REDACTED: code] — [REDACTED: (b)(5)] — with the code copied exactly, once. Unrelated text near the region MUST stay outside the marker.

✅ Sample — a redaction that prints its exemption code


Source: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), FOIA production document (public domain)

Under Cybercrime, a dashed box the height of eight bullets prints only (b)(5); the eight bullet glyphs remain in the margin, their text gone. The code and the surviving bullets are both content the page prints: the eight bullets stay as eight list items, and the code appears once, inside the marker, at the start of the redacted span.
